description:
FOUND AND FIXED s408 (Opus 5), by #363: the die made a malformed eval loud.

perl allows WHITESPACE between a quote-like operator and its delimiter, and the
delimiter is the first NON-space character:

    my $b = qq {interp $x here};        perl: "interp V here"
                                        PCL : "{interp V here}"   SILENT WRONG

PCL took the character right after `qq` -- the SPACE -- as the delimiter
(`$content =~ s/^qq(.)//` in Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm, and the same
hand-strip in Pl/PExpr/TokenUtils.pm), so the real delimiters stayed IN the
value.  PPI has always answered correctly (->string gives `interp $x here` for
all spellings); the fix is to ask it (CLAUDE.md 11).

ONLY THE INTERPOLATING FORM WAS WRONG: `qq {plain}` (no interpolation) and
`q {single}` go down a different path and were right, which is why this
survived -- the wrong value only appears when the string interpolates.

HOW IT SURFACED, and why it matters as a method note: perl-tests/index.t builds
an assertion with `qq {is (index ("$str", "$q"), $res, } . qq {"..."}` and
EVALS it.  With the braces left in, the eval text was `{is (index (...), }"..."`
-- unparseable.  Before #363 that eval dropped a statement SILENTLY and the
file scored 110/120 with 10 rows quietly missing; with #363's die the file's
own `die $@ if $@` aborted it at test 59, costing 61 rows.  So a loud failure
in one place (#363) exposed a silent wrong in another; the -61 was not the
flip's cost, it was this bug's.

POPULATION: THREE corpus files carried silently-wrong strings --
perl-tests/index.t, magic.t (`qq < @$_; ... >`, and `qq 'sub UNIVERSAL::...'`),
yadayada.t (an eval string again).  corpus-diff shows exactly those three,
every hunk the delimiters disappearing from a literal.

GUARDS: Pl/t/string-interp-01.t, four spellings (space+brace, no-space brace,
two spaces + paren, space + angle) plus the non-interpolating twins.
subject: SILENT WRONG (fixed s408): `qq {…}` with WHITESPACE before the delimiter kept the delimiters in the string value
